rationale: The target invariant that any unauthorized operation rejects the complete batch necessarily overlaps concrete-object authorization and stale-version atomicity.
A faithful sequential authorize-and-commit mutant also fails sibling stale-version/object-scope probes; singleton isolation was achievable only by conditioning mutant behavior on batch cardinality.
Cardinality-gated mutants are not the frozen planned mutants and would manufacture efficacy through probe partitioning rather than discriminate independent mechanisms.
The external-effect near miss could be made singleton only by omitting its prohibited effect from sibling rejection assertions.

experimental_matrix.warning: The apparent singleton result depended on rejected cardinality gates and effect-omitting sibling assertions.

review_blockers: Preflight mutant was activated only for batches of at least three operations.
Object-scope mutant was activated only for exactly two operations.
Sibling checks ignored effect-ledger changes to isolate the external-effect near miss.
Version-position probes did not establish general late-stale behavior or BEGIN IMMEDIATE concurrency semantics.
